brief:
Tonight is Pull A, and it is the first Pull A since you changed gyms on 2 September. That one fact drives almost everything below. The last time you ran this session was 28 August, in the old building, so every number this app would have printed on its own tonight was measured on machines you no longer use.

The one that mattered is the wide lat pulldown. Left alone, your card would have said 135 and then 150 twice. The only pulldown you have done in the new gym is the close grip on 3 September, where you worked up to 88. The same close-grip lift read 127.5 at the old gym three days before that. That is not a small difference, and 150 would have failed on the first set. So tonight the pulldown is 83 for ten, 88 for ten, then 94 for eight. Be straight with yourself about this one: 83 and 88 are pins you actually selected on 3 September, but 94 is my estimate of one notch above them, not something I read anywhere. If 94 is not a real pin on that tower, take the next one up, and log whatever the machine actually says. This is a calibration night. If it comes up easy, that is fine and it is the number I need.

Deadlift comes down. You have pulled 265 on three separate sessions — 24 July, 1 August and 28 August — and it has given you five reps every single time and never six. Repeating it would be the fourth run at the same wall. So the top set is 255, which you did get for six twice on 18 August, and there are three sets there instead of two: 245 for six, then 255 for six three times. That is 24 reps in the range tonight against 21 last time. 265 gets another try next Pull A off a stronger base. It has also been thirteen days since you last pulled, and this is the first lift of the night — warm up properly before the opener.

The seated cable row holds at 105 for twelve, four sets. Both trainers agreed on that one without argument. You earned the step to 112.5 on 28 August, and I am not spending it on a machine you have not touched since the move — take the reading tonight and the step is yours next time.

Dumbbell curls stay at 30 for three sets, but the ask is ten reps on all three instead of the nine you got last time. Get all three and the 35s are next. Cable hammer curls go up to 37.5 for ten, and face pulls go to 28.75 for twelve. Those two moves are safe because the cable stack came across the gym change unchanged — your face pulls read 27.5 in both buildings and your cable reverse curls read 37.5 in both.

Two things you should know. Your bodyweight has not been logged since 23 August, eighteen days ago, at 207, and it has been flat since 21 July. With the show on 1 March that is the one number nothing else in this app can work out for me. Step on the scale. And this review did not run yesterday — there is no 9 September packet in the repo, so your phone has been showing Monday's card for two days. Today's is live.

Two of the cards you were shown on Monday are gone, and you should know why rather than just finding them missing. The one asking to swap your Push A incline press for assisted dips is withdrawn: on 8 September you pressed a barbell for three sets of eight in that slot, so dips would have traded real load for bodyweight work you already do on Push B. The one asking to turn your Push B row into a cable row is withdrawn too, and it leaves a question I need you to answer — on 3 September you rowed four sets of eight in a slot still named for a smith machine, and unlike your incline press and your RDL you did not write down what you used. Tell me on the card next time and I can name that slot properly. Two cards remain on your plan screen, both renaming a smith slot to what you are actually doing.

One more thing worth your attention. You have not run Legs A once in this whole block — the last one was 20 August, three weeks ago, and the slot got skipped on 2 September during the gym move. Leg press with your feet low, Bulgarian split squats and leg extensions only exist on that day, so all three have had no work at all in the last fortnight while your deload starts on 21 September. I cannot move your rotation from here; that is the day-order setting on your own screen. If you want Legs A before the block ends, set it there.

Conditioning: easy cardio twice this week, twenty to thirty minutes.

flags.note: First Pull A since the gym change on 2 September. Left alone your card would have shown 150 on the wide pulldown; the only pulldown reading from the new gym is 88.

The top set of the wide pulldown, 94, is my estimate of one notch above the pins you used on 3 September — not a weight anyone has read on that machine. Take the nearest real pin and log what it says.
Deadlift 265 has given five reps and never six on three separate sessions. Tonight tops out at 255, which you have done for six.
Bodyweight last logged 23 August, eighteen days ago, at 207, and flat since 21 July. The show is on 1 March.
No review ran on 9 September — your phone showed Monday's card for two days. Today's is live.
Meso 2, week 3 of 4, a build block. All three trainers reported; five disagreements, all settled, and no injury objections.
Your recovery trainer wants it said plainly: if you accept the Legs B change below, you will be pulling a barbell off the floor twice a cycle. Answer No if that is more hinging than you want.
Your 3 September and 5 September sessions were entered in bulk, so their session lengths and rest times are not real timing and no trainer used them as evidence.

Legs A has not been run once this block — 21 days since 20 August. Leg press (feet low), Bulgarian split squats and leg extensions live only on that day and have zero sets in the last fortnight. Deload starts 21 September.

Three of your six sessions are named for a smith machine because the app's exercise list has no barbell press, barbell row or RDL in it. Adding one is a change to the app, not something any trainer here can put on a card.

Your 17 August question about corrective work is still open. There is no shoulder-rotation or anti-rotation movement anywhere in the exercise list, so there is no honest card to offer you — it needs the list itself changed.

Two of Monday's cards are withdrawn — the assisted-dips swap and the Pull B cable-row swap. On 3 September you did not write down what you rowed with; note it next time and that slot can be named properly.

proposals.why: On 2 September you pressed dumbbells in this slot and wrote "New gym. No smith machine. Dumbbell press", so this renames the Push B opener to the dumbbell shoulder press you are actually doing and asks for 4 sets of 8 to 10 instead of the smith bar's 6 to 8 — it will open at the weight you are already pressing on Push A, so nothing about the load changes, only the name and the rep ask.

You ran this slot with a barbell on 5 September and wrote "Barbell" on the card, so this renames the Legs B opener to the deadlift — the only barbell hinge anywhere in the app's exercise list — and keeps the same four sets at 8 to 10 reps, well clear of the heavy fives you pull on Pull A; note that accepting this means a barbell pull off the floor twice a cycle, which your recovery trainer wants you to weigh before you say Yes.

overrides.reason: 265 has given you five reps and never six, on 24 July, 1 August and 28 August. Repeating it is a fourth run at the same wall. 255 for six is proven — you did it twice on 18 August. So the opener goes up to 245 and the top comes down to 255 for three sets: 24 reps in range tonight against 21 last time. It has been thirteen days since you pulled, and this is the first lift of the night. Warm up properly.

This card would have said 150. That was measured at the old gym. The only pulldown you have done here is the close grip on 3 September — 77, 83, then 88 for ten — and the same lift read 127.5 at the old gym on 25 August. 83 and 88 are pins you actually selected on that tower. 94 is my estimate of one notch above, not a reading; if it is not a real pin, take the next one up. Log what the machine says. Tonight is for getting a true number, not defending an old one, and light is the right way to be wrong here.

You earned 112.5 on 28 August — twelve reps on all four sets at 105 — and I am not spending it on a machine you have not touched since the gym change. There is no row logged anywhere after 2 September, and the new gym's machines have not shifted by any one factor I could apply. Take the reading at 105 tonight and the step is yours next Pull A.

A 30-pound dumbbell weighs 30 pounds in any building, so this number survived the move intact. You got nine, nine and nine on 28 August in an eight-to-ten window. The next pair up is 35, which is a big jump off three sets that fell a rep short. Get ten on all three tonight and the 35s are next.

You hit twelve on all three sets at 35 on 28 August, the top of the window, so the pin moves. It moves here too because the cable stack came across the gym change unchanged — your cable reverse curls read 37.5 at the old gym on 25 August and 37.5 at the new one on 3 September. 37.5 is a real pin, no add-on needed. Reps back to ten and climb again.

The one lift tonight with a reading from inside this gym: 27.5 for fifteen twice on 3 September, and the same on 28 August before the move. Two sessions at the ceiling of the window earns the step. 28.75 is the 27.5 pin plus one 1.25-pound add-on. Two sets, which is the number you asked for on 28 August and were granted.

dissent.progression: Cut the top to 255 and add a third set there — 245/255/255/255 for six — because 265 has stalled at five reps across three sessions.
dissent.recovery: Hold and repeat 28 August exactly: 235 for six, then 255, 265 and 265 for five.
dissent.why: Ruling for progression here is also the safer card, which is why recovery loses its own argument. Recovery's stated worry is that the last increase cost reps and that he is thirteen days off the lift — but its prescription re-runs 265, the exact weight that cost those reps, twice. Progression's tops out ten pounds lower. Both seats agree nothing goes up tonight; only progression's version stops feeding a three-session stall, and 255 for six is documented on 18 August, so nothing here is a guess.

dissent.progression: Prescribe 83, 88 and 94 — anchored on pins he verifiably selected on the new tower on 3 September.
dissent.recovery: Emit no number at all. He sets the pin by feel with two reps in reserve and logs what it reads.
dissent.why: Recovery is right on the principle and I cannot deliver it. An override needs real weights; if I leave this slot empty the app falls back to standing rules and prints 150 — the old gym's number, roughly a third too heavy, and the single worst outcome available tonight. Between a number he can correct and a number that is definitely wrong, I take the correctable one. Progression's is built from pins he actually selected on 3 September and it deliberately errs light. I have put recovery's point on the card and in the notice bar instead: 94 is named as my estimate, not a reading, and he is told to take the nearest real pin and log it.

dissent.progression: Same 30, but ten reps on all three sets — the top of the window, which cashes into the 35s next time.
dissent.recovery: Same 30, nine reps, repeating what he did on 28 August.
dissent.why: The weight is identical on both sides, so nothing about load is in dispute and recovery filed no fatigue objection here. What is left is the rep ask, and the slot has asked eight to ten all along. He produced nine, nine and nine on 28 August. Asking for the tenth rep is asking him to finish the range he is already inside, not to take on anything new.

dissent.progression: Step the pin to 37.5 for ten, three sets — he hit twelve on all three at 35.
dissent.why: Recovery called this one a soft hold and said in as many words that if progression argued the next rung it should have it. It does argue it, and the evidence is clean: twelve reps on all three sets at 35 on 28 August is the ceiling of the window. The cable stack is also the one piece of hardware confirmed unchanged across the gym move, so 37.5 means here what it meant there.

dissent.progression: Step to 28.75 for twelve, two sets, off two sessions at the top of the rep window.
dissent.why: This is the only lift on tonight's card with a reading taken inside the new gym, so the usual argument for holding — that the number might be measuring the building rather than the man — does not apply. He did 27.5 for fifteen twice on 3 September here and twice on 28 August there. Two sessions pinned at the ceiling is what earns a step, and recovery offered no fatigue grounds against it, only caution. 28.75 is one 1.25-pound add-on above the pin, the smallest move available.
